no source carries cl, el, conf, so a club playing in Europe looks the same here as one that is not. This is the gap that produced the GW7 Triple Captain error

does_not_cover.what: the domestic cups (FA Cup, League Cup)
does_not_cover.why: no source carries them for the current season; they are also what creates blanks and doubles, so this matters more from GW20

does_not_cover.what: injury updates between now and the deadline
does_not_cover.why: `news` is a snapshot of what FPL had when the pipeline ran, not a feed

does_not_cover.what: WHEN a due price change will happen
does_not_cover.why: FPL's price system is rolling rather than nightly -- locks land across the day -- and `price_change_hourly_rate` does not reconcile with the published projections in any units, so no countdown can be derived from it honestly

calendar.honesty: This is TIME and MONEY awareness. It is not football awareness. An empty calendar means Gaffer knows of nothing pending in the things it can see -- it does not mean no team news is coming.

wait_vs_act.not_an_evpi: This does not price the information and does not compute an optimal time to act. It puts the edge beside what is pending and reports both in their own units.
wait_vs_act.reason: Cherki is close to a price change by FPL's own figure but is not due, and no timing can be derived -- so this is a risk of waiting, not a cost of it
wait_vs_act.no_exchange_rate: Money and points are reported separately and deliberately not combined: 0.1m of team value has no fixed worth in expected points, and inventing a rate to produce one number would be a made-up precision.
wait_vs_act.missing_term: The football information -- team news, press conferences, predicted lineups -- is NOT in this comparison, and on most weeks it is the larger term. See the calendar's `does_not_cover`.

assumptions: Move and hold are scored in the same 2000 fixture scenarios, with the same projections, objective and team state.
The hold baseline re-optimises your XI and captain from the squad you already own (source: GW5), so it is the best version of doing nothing.
Horizon value uses gameweeks 2-6, where Gaffer's mean projections are materially weaker than its one-week ones.

The bar for calling a move an action (1.0 points and 55% chance of beating the hold) is a conservative policy choice, not a fitted one. It becomes fittable once ~6 gameweeks of decision snapshots and reviews exist.

largest_weak_component.evidence: Brier 0.1899 against a league base rate of 0.1901 -- barely distinguishable from quoting the base rate to everybody -- and over-confident above 0.35, where a claimed 0.49 realises 0.29. A reconciled two-pass alternative was built and measured and lost on the decision metric

evidence_quality.policy: which statuses count as weak evidence is a DECLARED POLICY CHOICE, not a fitted threshold; the statuses themselves come from measurements recorded in backtest.py

comparison.delta_range_means: the spread of FOOTBALL outcomes for this move against this hold, across the same shared scenarios. Unlike delta_ci95 it does not shrink when more scenarios are drawn.

domain.horizon_delta: gameweeks 2 onward of the planning horizon, where the mean projections are materially weaker than the one-week ones

threshold_status.rationale: A conservative floor that stops a sub-point projected edge — well inside any honest model's error — from being published as a transfer recommendation. It is not derived from a measurement.
threshold_status.withdrawn_justification: The original 1.0 was justified by a ~0.76 rank correlation and ~85 legal-XI points per gameweek. Both came from baselines withdrawn in T-26 and are no longer cited.
threshold_status.reassess_after: a pre-registered sample-and-power requirement, computed in `gaffer.loop.fitting_readiness` and measured in DISCORDANT decisions rather than gameweeks. The previously published '~6 completed gameweeks' was inherited without scrutiny and is wrong by roughly two orders of magnitude; the bars stay declared policy until the computed requirement is met, very possibly beyond this season.
